claims.claim: Every g_(n,e) is an integral polynomial and equals the indicated coefficient of the formal inverse.
The exact weighted-Euler syzygy (4.3) holds in Z[x_1,...,x_e].
In the x_1 non-zero chart and appropriate residue characteristic, the LPS determinant condition is equivalent to a smooth-point plus next-coefficient condition.
A simple finite-field common zero with non-zero next coefficient gives a complex LPS specialisation; p need not avoid d+e-1.
The scheme-theoretic smooth-curve, reduced-affine-zero-divisor hypotheses imply the required Jacobian point.
A coefficient-one closed point over a perfect ground field becomes a reduced geometric collection after base change and satisfies the curve bridge under the stated support conditions.
For every n >= 2, every zero of the e=3 one-variable boundary factor P_n is real, positive and simple.
All 51 frozen witnesses for 50 <= d <= 100 satisfy the legacy and refactored relations.
For 2 <= d <= 20, (G_d,G_(d+1)) is reduced of length floor(d(d+1)/6), and J_d and G_(d+2) are units in its coordinate algebra.
For 2 <= d <= 200 the adjacent boundary torus factors are coprime.
Lewis-Perry-Straub Theorem 4 converts the complex specialisation into the stated Polydegree containment.
The uniform all-d e=3 radicality, Jacobian-unit and next-coefficient-unit statement holds.
A bounded collision search found no prior derivative-Jacobian packaging; novelty and priority are not established.
No independent reproduction, formal verification, external specialist review or peer review has been established.
